conversions._note: All 16 gated fixtures, not the three the task required, at the shipping RAW profile (pdfium/standard/none/refine0@240dpi) -- the product's own serialisation path with only the oracle removed, because an oracle is an environment fact and this proof must not need one. the_cost_of_not_installing_the_extra._note: THE FINDING OF THIS PROOF, and it is not a comfortable one. The quality ladder is default-ON since c9d36df and needs base-14 text metrics that only MuPDF supplies in this tree. A default install therefore runs an INERT ladder. This section measures what that costs instead of asserting it is small, because on the exemplar document it is not.
the_cost_of_not_installing_the_extra.mechanism: `get_metrics('mupdf')` degrades to NullMetrics, `predict_lines` returns None for every paragraph, and `apply_ladder` locks nothing. Reported, not silent: `ladder_report['text_metrics']` is 'none' and --verbose prints it.

fidelity_comparison._note: Same commit, same parser, same RAW profile, same 16 inputs, same measuring instrument -- the ONLY difference is whether the `mupdf` extra was installed in the environment that produced the DOCX. Scored with testkit/harness.py from /work/.venv in both cases; harness.py needs PyMuPDF by design and must not share an implementation with the parser it measures, so the converter under test and the oracle are deliberately different installs.

assessment.why_not: Gate (c) asks whether a PyMuPDF-free install exists, installs and works. It does: 16 of 16 fixtures convert to valid DOCX, 25 of 25 modules import, and the absent backend fails with a typed error naming the extra. The degradation is bounded to 3 of 16 documents, is caused by an optional quality pass declining to run rather than by anything being broken, and is reported by the product itself.
assessment.but: It is a RELEASE concern and should not be filed as a footnote. c1_whitepaper is the standing exemplar for the ordinary-document release bar, and without the extra its raw-lane within2pt returns to 0.0000 -- the exact pathology commit c9d36df was written to remove. l1_word_native, a PDF printed from a word processor, loses dy_p50 3.31 -> 11.04. Both are squarely the document class this converter exists for.
assessment.and_the_sharper_version: The gate baseline is recorded in an environment that HAS the extra, because the measurement container installs it to run the parity reference arm. So the published product numbers describe a configuration a default `pip install exactdoc` does not produce. Nothing here is wrong, and the profile_id does not carry a text-metrics axis to say so. Naming it is the point; fixing it is a permissive shaper in exactdoc/metrics.py, which is release work, not migration work.

tests_without_the_extra._note: 'A test suite that cannot run without the AGPL extra would undermine the claim.' Run against the INSTALLED wheel: the tree was staged without `exactdoc/` so that the `sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)` every test file performs cannot shadow site-packages with the source copy.
tests_without_the_extra.command: cd <tree without exactdoc/> && python -m unittest discover -s tests

the_measurement_toolkit.reason: All four reach `testkit/harness.py`, which imports fitz at module level. That is a DESIGN constraint, not an oversight: the harness must not share an implementation with the parser it scores, or a parser that mis-groups a page would mis-group it identically on both sides and score itself perfect. PDFium is now the shipping parser, so the independent instrument has to be PyMuPDF.
the_measurement_toolkit.consequence: The measurement toolkit is AGPL-governed and the shipped converter is not. Nothing under exactdoc/ imports harness.py.

the_quality_ladder.reason: Every question is downstream of `ladder.predict_lines`, which needs base-14 metrics. Without them the predicate is constant, so these tests would not measure a weaker ladder -- they would measure an absent one.

cross_backend_comparison.reason: They compare the two parsers; one arm is not installed.

tests_without_the_extra.the_guards_were_broken_and_this_is_how_i: Six of these already carried `try: from exactdoc.parse import parse_pdf / except ImportError: = None`. That guard worked only because parse.py had a top-level `import fitz`. Making it lazy -- the change that empties the seam -- also made every one of those guards a no-op: the module imports fine and raises at call time, so they bound a live function and the failure moved into the assertion, where it read as a product defect. The first run of this proof measured 13 failures and 24 errors, and that is how the defect surfaced. `tests/mupdf_extra.py` now asks the question by probing `parse.require_fitz()` -- the same door the product uses, so the guard cannot disagree with the code it guards.

licence_after_the_swap._note: Re-verified after the LICENSE commit, in a SECOND clean virtualenv built from a wheel rebuilt out of the relicensed tree. Only the metadata half of this proof was re-run, and deliberately so: the licence commit changed no code under exactdoc/, so the conversions, the module imports and the test run above are unaffected by it. What the swap CAN change is what a licence scan of the environment reports, and that is what was pending.

wheel_metadata.Classifier: License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License

licence_after_the_swap._the_claim_now_holds_without_an_exclusio: The first scan reported `agpl_packages: ['exactdoc']` -- exactdoc's own still-AGPL declaration -- and the claim had to be stated as 'no THIRD-PARTY AGPL package'. It no longer needs the qualifier: the scan finds no AGPL term anywhere in the environment, including on exactdoc itself. Three statements of the same fact were checked rather than one, because any of them can be updated alone: the wheel's METADATA, its classifier, and the LICENSE file bundled inside it. A wheel whose metadata says Apache-2.0 while its bundled LICENSE is the AGPL text ships a contradiction to every user, and neither half looks wrong on its own. `tests/test_packaging_metadata.py::test_the_declared_licence_is_the_migration_target` now asserts all three.
